answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, assigning each identity voting weight from normalized visit probability. A sybil cluster may add many internal edges, but a sparse boundary cut gives it low conductance; min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore limit escape and incoming probability, mathematically capping its aggregate vote. Attestations tied to basalt, yarrow, and quartz identities remain costly to fabricate.
